claims.text: A file-based approach stores each application's data in its own files, separate from every other application's, with no shared store between them.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Data duplication in a file-based approach wastes storage and lets copies disagree: a value changed in one file leaves the other files' copies stale, because the same data is held in several places.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Program-data dependency means a change to a file's structure forces changes to every program that uses the file, because each program reads the file by its layout.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A relational database stores data in tables that applications share, with each value held once, so duplication and disagreeing copies are removed at their source.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The DBMS sits between the applications and the data, so programs ask for data by table and attribute rather than by file layout, and a change to the storage is absorbed without changes to every program.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: An entity is what a table stores data about; a table holds one entity's data; a record in the table (a tuple) is one row; an attribute (a field) is one column.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A primary key is the attribute or attributes whose value identifies each record uniquely; a candidate key is any attribute that could serve as the primary key; a secondary key is an attribute used to search a table that does not identify a record uniquely.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A foreign key is an attribute in one table that is the primary key of another table, and it links the two.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A one-to-many relationship links one record of the first table to many of the second; a one-to-one links one to one; a many-to-many links many to many in both directions and is implemented as two one-to-many relationships through a link table.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Referential integrity means a foreign key's value must match a primary key value in the referenced table, so a record cannot point at a record that does not exist.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: An index is a structure the DBMS keeps over a table's search attribute that lets records be found without reading the whole table.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: An entity-relationship (E-R) diagram documents a database design: a box for each entity and a labelled line for each relationship, with the relationship's kind (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many) marked on the line.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: First Normal Form (1NF) means a table has no repeating groups: each field holds a single value and a primary key identifies each record.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Second Normal Form (2NF) means 1NF and no non-key attribute depends on only part of a composite primary key.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Third Normal Form (3NF) means 2NF and no non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute: every non-key attribute depends on the key, the whole key and nothing but the key.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Testing for 3NF runs the definitions in order - repeating groups for 1NF, part-key dependencies for 2NF, then non-key-to-non-key dependencies for 3NF - and the first failure names the form the table is stuck at.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Producing a normalised design works table by table: identify the entity, give it a primary key, move each repeating group into its own table with a foreign key back, and move attributes that depend on something other than the key into the table of the thing they depend on.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).
